campaigns.title: A test that rewrites a gate baseline fails, and the guard is actually reached

mutants.breaks: the guard becomes opt-in, so it protects only tests that ask for it and none of the ones nobody has written yet. The most important mutant in this campaign: an opt-in guard passes every test in the repo forever, and only the wiring test can see it
rewrites are detected and then ignored, which is exactly as useful as not detecting them

the one case that actually happened — same file, new content — is never reported. Chosen to fail CLOSED: the obvious mutant here inverts `!=` to `==`, which reports every UNCHANGED baseline instead, so the autouse guard then errors sixteen tests in teardown and the runner reads the whole run as BROKEN. Mutating a suite-wide fixture is self-referential; the mutant has to make the guard miss things, never invent them
a gate whose baseline has vanished has nothing left to ratchet against, and the guard says nothing

two empty snapshots compare equal, so moving or deleting scripts/baselines/ disarms the guard on every test without a single failure — the TECH-032 shape, where a checker that cannot find its subject reports success

a rewrite with identical bytes becomes invisible. Not academic: `record_run` rewrites the mutation ledger byte-identically whenever it has nothing to report, so `test_mutation_nightly.py` overwrote it on every suite run and the content-only first draft of this guard stayed silent — it would have spoken only on the day a finding existed, which is the one day the file's contents matter

every write is still caught, but each is reported as 'rewritten with identical content' — so the message that says a gate's standard MOVED is never printed, and the reader is told the harmless version of the truth
